base-fixed-profile.phase_mapping_basis: single instance; 30 sequential events = 30 sequential step intervals; no unmapped kernels; 48 target names exactly once per interval; profiler-end minus event-complete offset stable within reported spread; first 10 warmup, next 20 measured

fusion-fixed-profile.phase_mapping_basis: single instance; 30 sequential events = 30 sequential step intervals; no unmapped kernels; 48 target names exactly once per interval; profiler-end minus event-complete offset stable within reported spread; first 10 warmup, next 20 measured

limitations: One short profiled A/B pair; kernel diagnostics are not independent formal QPS/p99 acceptance.
Task durations can overlap and their sums are not wall-clock latency; Task Wait Time is not summed as kernel work.
No output-port memory-write volume conclusion follows from four fused output descriptors.
No proof that core count is optimal or that fusion helps all shapes/concurrency configurations.
Profiler timestamps use their own clock; ordinal phase mapping is supported by interval/task counts and near-constant completion offset, not equality of absolute clocks.
No matched final GE dump was captured; residual-Add edge uses the unchanged packed ONNX and names from actual profiling plus the loaded pass/replacement log.
